newsitem.title: UK: British sugar beet plantings due to start soon.
newsitem.headline: British sugar beet plantings due to start soon.

text.p: Sugar beet sowings for Britain's 1997/98 crop are expected to start soon and cover about the same area as last season, analysts said on Wednesday.

"We would hope that the growers will drill as early as conditions allow. It's all down to the weather, the seed beds are pretty good," said an official at British Sugar. Beet planting trials have already started.
"We would have thought they'll be making a start fairly soon," he said, adding that there would be a month-long opportunity for plantings, starting from this week.
Area was about 170,000 hectares last year, the same as in 1995/96, and is expected to remain broadly unchanged for 1997/98.
The National Farmers' Union (NFU) said sales of beet seeds were progressing as normal although the list of varieties available to growers had seen some adjustments.
"The recommended list of varieties has changed since last year...certain varieties had to be exchanged due to insufficient quantities," said an official at the NFU.
But all seeds on offer were similar in terms of sugar content and yield, she said.
Earlier this week, trade house ED&F Man estimated Britain's white sugar production at 1.47 million tonnes raw value in 1996/97, up from a previous 1.33 million.
